LESSON: THE CELL

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: GENERAL SCIENCE
Strand: Life Science 1.1 Introduction to General Science (8 lessons) ● Importance of Gen
Topic 1.2: The Cell
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 8

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers The Cell, part of Life Science 1.1 Introduction to General Science (8 lessons) ● Importance of Gen in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10 GENERAL SCIENCE.

Key inquiry question: How are light and electron microscopes used in day-to-day life?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. discuss with peers the differences between light and electron microscopes. Learners with speech difficulties could use alternative modes of communication to express their views,

2. use print or non-print media to search for the structures of plant and animal cells under electron microscope and share the information. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use adapted digital devices to conduct research. Screen resolution could be regulated for learners with photophobia such as those with epilepsy or

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. discuss with peers the differences between light and electron microscopes. Learners with speech difficulties could use alternative modes of communication to express their views,
2. use print or non-print media to search for the structures of plant and animal cells under electron microscope and share the information. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use adapted digital devices to conduct research. Screen resolution could be regulated for learners with photophobia such as those with epilepsy or

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on The Cell together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Creativity and Imagination: as the learner constructs models of plant and animal cells as seen under the electron and

light microscopes.

● Digital literacy: as the learner searches for information from the internet on the structure of a cell as seen under the

electron microscope.

● Learning to learn: as the learner reflects on the project work and adjusts appropriately.

Values:
● Respect: as the learner considers others’ opinion while working on practical activities in groups such as construction of

models.

● Social justice: as the learner seeks equity, equality and gender consideration in distribution of learning resources such

as sharing of materials for making cell models.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

● Environmental conservation: as the learner manages wastes responsibly to avoid pollution while preparing plant and

animal cell models.

● Safety and security: as the learner observes safety precautions when preparing the models.

Suggested Learning Resources:

Text books, Light microscope, Charts showing electron microscopes, Photomicrographs of plant and animal cells, Manilla

papers, locally available materials, Online resources, educational videos, adapted digital devices, adapted writing

resources, Equipped biology laboratory,

Other Related Service Providers: Physiotherapists, Occupational Therapists, Learner Support Assistants, Speech

Therapists, Nurse,
